guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not reacting against Missouri simply because the opener was lopsided. Missouri produced 562 yards in a 54-14 win, while Austin Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards and four touchdowns. That performance showed the offense can be efficient, but one game against Arkansas-Pine Bluff does not fully resolve the uncertainty surrounding a new starting quarterback, a new offensive coordinator and a unit that returned only five starters.

For us, the case for Troy is less about expecting offensive success and more about questioning how much separation Missouri should be expected to create. Our numbers give Missouri clear advantages against a Troy offense that has struggled to generate efficient passing plays and consistent scoring opportunities. The meaningful counterweight is that Missouri replaced 10 starters from last season’s defense, making it difficult to treat the current unit as fully established despite a strong opening performance. We think the market is charging too much for Missouri’s likely control of the game.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
The matchup we are watching is Troy’s passing offense against Missouri’s pass defense. Missouri held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 109 passing yards and a 23 percent third-down conversion rate, and our longer-run numbers also favor the defense here. Troy’s challenge is not necessarily producing explosive offense; it is avoiding repeated empty possessions that allow Missouri to build the margin quickly.

That is also the biggest concern for our position. If Troy cannot stay functional through the air, Missouri’s defensive advantage can overwhelm the broader case for taking the points. We still see enough uncertainty in Missouri’s rebuilt defense to believe the available cushion matters.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 home win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on September 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, and converted 6 of 10 third downs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime after outgaining the Golden Lions 376-6 in the first half.
Missouri's defense held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards and forced five three-and-outs.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri is scheduled to host Troy at 6 p.m. CT on September 19, 2026.
Missouri offensive coordinator Chip Lindsey was Troy's head coach from 2019 through 2021.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons is Missouri's starting quarterback on the current depth chart.
Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in his Missouri debut against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Simmons' 89.5 percent completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were Missouri records for a quarterback making his program debut.
Sophomore Matt Zollers is listed as Simmons' backup and completed 8 of 12 passes for 87 yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri lost 2025 starting quarterback Beau Pribula and added transfers Austin Simmons and Nick Evers to a quarterback room that also includes Zollers.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's listed first-team offensive line is LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025 and lost six, including quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison and tackles Keagan Trost.
Left tackle Cayden Green, center Dominick Giudice and right guard Curtis Peagler are 2026 captains.
Green allowed two sacks, two quarterback hits and three hurries over 750 snaps in 2025, according to PFF.
Senior Jamal Roberts is listed as the starting running back and rushed 13 times for 47 yards and a touchdown in the opener.
Wide receiver Donovan Olugbode recorded career highs of seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee is a listed starting receiver and caught five passes for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown, in his Missouri debut.
Starting tight end Brett Norfleet led Missouri with five receiving touchdowns in 2025 and entered 2026 tied for fifth among Missouri tight ends with 10 career touchdown receptions.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned two defensive starters and lost 10 from its 2025 defense.
Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez and safety Santana Banner ranked second and third on Missouri in tackles in 2025 and are listed as starters in 2026.
Missouri added SEC transfer starters Robert Woodyard Jr. at linebacker and Chris Graves Jr. at cornerback.
Woodyard started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded 67 tackles, including 50 in conference play.
Graves appeared in 41 games over three seasons at Ole Miss and started nine games in 2025.
Defensive tackles Sterling Webb and Marquis Gracial combined for 6.0 tackles for loss in 2025; Webb also recorded 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Darris Smith recorded four sacks as a pass-rush specialist in 2025 and is listed as Missouri's starting JACK defender in 2026.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 and is coaching from the booth.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026.
Alex Atkins joined Missouri as tight ends coach in January 2026 after serving as LSU's tight ends coach and run-game coordinator in 2025.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator duties before the 2026 season while continuing to coach linebackers.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, ranking eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri had a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances and scored 31 rushing touchdowns in 2025.
In the 2026 opener, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60 percent of its third downs and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone possessions.
Three Missouri receivers caught touchdown passes from Simmons in the opener: Shaun Terry II, Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, ranking eighth nationally in total defense and 17th in scoring defense.
The 2025 defense allowed 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
Missouri held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 89 rushing yards, 109 passing yards and a 23 percent third-down conversion rate in the 2026 opener.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig is Missouri's starting placekicker and made a 32-yard field goal plus all seven extra-point attempts against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Florida State transfer Brunno Reus is listed as Missouri's starting punter, kickoff specialist and holder.
DaMarion Fowlkes is listed as Missouri's primary punt and kickoff returner and had a 23-yard punt return in the opener.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri has won 15 consecutive regular-season nonconference games dating to September 17, 2022.
Missouri has won 24 consecutive home games against non-SEC opponents dating to October 21, 2017.
Missouri has won 12 consecutive home night games dating to November 19, 2022.
Missouri is 34-9 at home under head coach Eli Drinkwitz.
